title: Mixed workload trace analysis (anonymized) — prompt/context length distributions + short/long threshold sensitivity
body:
Purpose
- Working sheet to summarize prompt/context length distributions from anonymized traces and to sanity-check candidate thresholds for the short/long prompt-aware scheduler policy.
- This is NOT a full performance model; used to pick reasonable default knobs for Phase 1 and define sensitivity ranges for benchmarks.

Data sources + anonymization
- Sources: sampled runtime request logs + trace replay export (Hosted API + a small number of Dedicated pools).
- Sampling: 1–5% request sampling depending on pool; all samples are request-level and anonymized.
- Token counts: runtime tokenizer (model-specific) applied to prompt; “context_tokens” = prompt_tokens + cached_prefix_tokens when available (approx; see notes).
- Exclusions: requests with missing token metadata; streaming partials where TTFT not recorded.
- Time range: 2025-09-29 → 2025-10-06 (weekday-heavy; one weekend day included)

Definitions (used below)
- prompt_tokens: tokens in the user-provided prompt for the request.
- cached_prefix_tokens: tokens served from prefix cache (best-effort approximation from cache hit metadata).
- context_tokens: prompt_tokens + cached_prefix_tokens.
- prefill_tokens: prompt_tokens (NOTE: if prefix cache hit, prefill cost is less than raw prompt_tokens; we track separately because scheduler classification might use a “predicted prefill cost” later).

Tab: TRACE SUMMARY (by source slice)
(Values are percentiles across requests within the slice)

| slice_id | env | region | pool_type | model_family | n_requests | prompt_tokens p50 | p90 | p95 | p99 | context_tokens p50 | p95 | p99 | cached_prefix_hit_rate | est_prefill_ms p50 | p95 | ttft_ms p50 | p95 | notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| HST-A | hosted | us-east | shared | llama-3.1-8b | 1,284,112 | 92 | 210 | 298 | 612 | 140 | 420 | 1,020 | 0.18 | 18 | 61 | 145 | 410 | chat-heavy; short prompts dominate; long tail present due to RAG + history |
| HST-B | hosted | us-east | shared | llama-3.1-70b | 412,778 | 118 | 260 | 390 | 910 | 210 | 680 | 1,720 | 0.11 | 32 | 118 | 230 | 760 | more long-context due to enterprise tenants; lower cache hit |
| HST-C | hosted | eu-west | shared | mixtral-8x7b | 596,004 | 84 | 188 | 260 | 540 | 130 | 390 | 940 | 0.21 | 16 | 55 | 132 | 365 | similar to HST-A but slightly tighter p95 |
| DED-1 | dedicated | us-east | dp-17 (isolation) | llama-3.1-70b | 92,114 | 160 | 520 | 880 | 2,050 | 420 | 1,980 | 5,120 | 0.06 | 44 | 210 | 310 | 1,480 | customer workload: long system prompts + multi-turn; worst mix for HoL blocking |
| DED-2 | dedicated | us-west | dp-09 (isolation) | qwen2.5-32b | 74,883 | 110 | 340 | 620 | 1,420 | 260 | 1,210 | 3,880 | 0.09 | 28 | 160 | 210 | 1,120 | moderate long tail; bursts (cron-style) observed |
| DED-3 | dedicated | eu-central | dp-05 (isolation) | llama-3.1-8b | 138,402 | 70 | 200 | 310 | 900 | 120 | 720 | 2,100 | 0.14 | 14 | 92 | 120 | 680 | smaller model but very long contexts at p99; cache hit higher but noisy |

Interpretation (quick)
- Hosted slices look mostly “short” by prompt length (p95 ~ 260–390), but context_tokens p99 can be > 1k because of cached prefix + long histories.
- Dedicated slices have a meaningfully heavier tail (prompt p95 ~ 620–880; context p99 up to ~5k in DED-1).
- This supports a classification threshold in the ~256–512 prompt token range for Hosted defaults, but Dedicated likely needs a higher threshold OR a different classifier (e.g., predicted prefill cost / context).

Tab: HISTOGRAM (coarse buckets)
(% of requests by prompt_tokens bucket; bucket edges: 0–64, 65–128, 129–256, 257–512, 513–1024, 1025–2048, >2048)

| slice_id | 0-64 | 65-128 | 129-256 | 257-512 | 513-1024 | 1025-2048 | >2048 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| HST-A | 28.4% | 33.6% | 24.1% | 10.7% | 2.6% | 0.5% | 0.1% |
| HST-B | 16.9% | 25.1% | 26.8% | 19.2% | 8.9% | 2.5% | 0.6% |
| HST-C | 30.1% | 34.2% | 23.0% | 10.0% | 2.1% | 0.5% | 0.1% |
| DED-1 | 6.1% | 10.4% | 19.8% | 25.6% | 23.9% | 11.6% | 2.6% |
| DED-2 | 9.2% | 15.7% | 24.9% | 24.0% | 17.0% | 7.5% | 1.7% |
| DED-3 | 18.8% | 23.6% | 28.7% | 17.0% | 7.6% | 3.3% | 1.0% |

Takeaways
- Hosted: setting “short <= 256 prompt tokens” classifies ~86% (HST-A/C) and ~69% (HST-B) as short.
- Dedicated: “short <= 256” classifies only ~36–71% as short depending on customer (DED-1 is only ~36%).

Tab: THRESHOLD SENSITIVITY (prompt_tokens-based)
Assumes baseline classifier = prompt_tokens <= threshold → short, else long.

| threshold (prompt_tokens) | HST-A %short | HST-B %short | DED-1 %short | DED-2 %short | comments |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 128 | 62.0% | 42.0% | 16.5% | 24.9% | too strict for Dedicated; long queue becomes huge, defeats purpose |
| 192 | 74.8% | 54.1% | 26.9% | 40.6% | still long-heavy on DED-1 |
| 256 | 86.1% | 68.8% | 36.3% | 49.8% | good Hosted split; Dedicated still heavy long tail |
| 320 | 90.8% | 74.9% | 42.8% | 56.7% | candidate “single default” if we accept more short on Dedicated |
| 384 | 93.5% | 79.4% | 48.7% | 62.4% | reduces long queue pressure; may reduce benefits vs true short-prioritization |
| 512 | 96.8% | 85.7% | 58.4% | 73.4% | too permissive for Hosted; risks reintroducing HoL blocking for “medium” prompts |

Notes / guidance to scheduling team
- For Hosted: 256–320 looks like the right range to get a meaningful short class while still carving out a long class that contains the worst offenders.
- For Dedicated: one-size threshold is risky. DED-1 shows a massive mid/long segment (257–1024) that will still interfere with short requests if classified as short.
- Recommendation for prototype: keep prompt_tokens threshold configurable per pool/model; start with 256 Hosted / 384 Dedicated for initial benchmark sweeps (to be validated).

Tab: THRESHOLD SENSITIVITY (context_tokens-based)
Motivation: prompt can be small but context (history) large; some of these still behave “long” at prefill because attention scales with total context.

| threshold (context_tokens) | HST-A %short | HST-B %short | DED-1 %short | comments |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 512 | 77.4% | 60.8% | 21.9% | catches long-history chats; Dedicated remains long-heavy |
| 768 | 86.6% | 70.9% | 31.0% | comparable to prompt<=256 in Hosted; still strict for DED-1 |
| 1024 | 92.2% | 78.2% | 39.8% | starts looking like prompt<=320/384 for Hosted |
| 1536 | 96.0% | 84.9% | 50.6% | permissive; may under-separate in Hosted |

Open question
- Classifier should likely be “predicted prefill cost” not raw tokens. Next step: add a derived column approximating prefill FLOPs or prefill_ms from runtime telemetry and redo sensitivity.

Tab: CANDIDATE DEFAULTS (for benchmark sweeps)
These are NOT final defaults; meant to constrain Phase 2 benchmark search.

| deployment | starting_threshold_basis | starting_threshold | rationale | must-measure |
|---|---|---:|---|---|
| Hosted API (shared pools) | prompt_tokens | 256 | creates clear separation; short class is ~70–86% across Hosted slices | short p95 queue time, long p95 progression, overall throughput |
| Dedicated (most pools) | prompt_tokens | 384 | avoids making “long” too dominant; still isolates worst >384 | long starvation counters, head-of-line reduction on mixed traces |
| Dedicated (long-context-heavy customers) | context_tokens | 768 | catches long-history/chat workloads even if prompt not huge | TTFT/p95 and aging effectiveness under sustained short load |

Notes to self / follow-ups
- Add another column: “prefill_ms estimated from runtime metrics” and recompute distributions by prefill_ms. (Owner: Claire; ask Logan for telemetry field mapping.)
- Verify whether cached_prefix_tokens is reliable enough; if not, drop context_tokens analysis and focus on prompt_tokens + observed prefill_ms.
- Need to compare these distributions to synthetic mixes (80/20, 50/50, long-spike) to ensure we’re not anchoring too hard on one week of traces.

Changelog
- 2025-10-07: initial import of HST-A + DED-1; draft bucket histogram.
- 2025-10-11: added HST-B/HST-C and Dedicated slices DED-2/DED-3; added context-based sensitivity tab.
- 2025-10-18: updated percentile calculations to exclude missing TTFT rows; corrected cached_prefix_hit_rate computation (was counting “unknown” as miss).
